1.0.0.en: The Apostle Paul begins by writing the sender of the epistle, who is Paul himself, and in humility he mentions his two disciples as partners with him, namely Silas and Timothy, although he alone is its writer; or he may have dictated it to them, or they only heard the thoughts that he wrote down and shared with him the feeling for the Church of Thessalonica. Then he writes the name of those to whom it is sent, who are the Church of the Thessalonians, that is, the community of believers in Thessalonica.

1.0.1.en: Our Father: The Apostle wants to affirm the personal bond between us and God, for He is our Father, especially as they are suffering afflictions, and God's fatherhood supports them.

1.0.2.en: And when he says in God and in the Lord Jesus Christ, he affirms the meaning that they have come out of the worship of idols to the worship of the true God, and that the Lord Jesus Christ is their Lord.

1.1.0.en: Paul sends his usual greeting at the beginning of every epistle, in which he shows that we need the grace of God to support us and keep us on our way each new day, and likewise we need peace from God that is not affected by the changing circumstances around us.

1.1.1.en: Your feeling of God's fatherhood toward you reassures you and supports you, and even urges you to work with strength. So always remember His fatherhood when you pray the Lord's Prayer, and ask for His help in every need, confident of His nearness to you and His care for even your smallest problems.

1.2.0.en: When the Apostle sees the growth of faith and love among the people of Thessalonica, he returns thanks to God, because it is He who works in them. The growth of their faith is due to their awareness of the Lord's support for them in the midst of afflictions and troubles, and that He hastens to give help and grace. The increase of love is the fruit of true, active faith: the more our faith grows, the more our love for others increases.

1.3.0.en: Paul encourages the Thessalonians and praises them for their patience in the persecutions that they endure from the Jews around them; indeed, out of his abundant joy in their patience he tells the other churches of the strength of their faith and boasts of them.

1.4.0.en: The Apostle continues to encourage them to endure afflictions, because this endurance is what confirms their worthiness of the heavenly Kingdom; for God is just, and He rewards everyone who loves Him and endures suffering for His sake with unspeakable blessings in heaven.

1.4.1.en: Be assured that all you endure in your dealings with others is of great value to God, and He will surely reward you for it in the Kingdom, because it is the proof of your love for Him and for others. Likewise, your endurance confirms the vanity of the world and of material things in your eyes, and your concern for heaven. So do not be troubled by the faults of others toward you, and pray for them, for these wrongs qualify you for the eternal inheritance.

1.5.0.en: At the awesome Second Coming of Christ, with the angels around Him, He will repay the wicked with just punishment, for the wrongdoer must pay the price of his wrongdoing; that is, He will repay with affliction those who persecuted the saints, while His own will have rest, joy and glory at His Second Coming as a just reward for the sufferings they endured.

1.6.0.en: Do not know God: They refused to know God by resisting the proclamation of Christ offered to them, or by neglecting it.

1.6.1.en: Paul affirms the punishment of the wicked who refused to know God and to obey the Gospel offered to them, and this punishment will be torment in the eternal fire.

1.7.0.en: From the face of the Lord and from the glory of His power: They will be deprived of God forever, and this is a torment in itself, in addition to the punishment of their sins.

1.7.1.en: The punishment of the wicked will be separation from God and eternal destruction.

1.8.0.en: To be glorified in His saints: He gives His glory and majesty to those who believe in Him.

1.8.1.en: To be admired in all those who believe: The wondrous glory of God appears in the greatness of His children in the Kingdom. Our testimony among you was believed: The truth of the proclamation of the Apostle Paul in Thessalonica appears in God's glorifying of everyone among them who believed.

1.8.2.en: In that day: The day of judgment and of entering the Kingdom.

1.8.3.en: The Apostle declares the truth of his proclamation, which will be made manifest on the last day when God glorifies His children in the Kingdom.

1.8.4.en: The glory of the Kingdom encourages us to endure sufferings and to count the delights of the world as nothing. At the same time, the eternal torment on the day of judgment makes us fear God and refuse every sin, however small it may seem, so that we may be saved on that great day and enjoy fellowship with God forever.

1.9.s.en: (4) The growth of God's work in the believers

1.9.0.en: Count you worthy of this calling: You respond to the proclamation of Christ.

1.9.1.en: Fulfil all the good pleasure of His goodness: Since you have received the faith, He completes His work in you so that you may do good works that gladden His heart and gladden you.

1.9.2.en: The work of faith with power: Faith bears fruit in you in good works and steadfastness before persecutions. Paul prays for the believers in Thessalonica that they may respond to his preaching and submit to the work of the Holy Spirit in them, so that their faith may be established and He may make them grow in every good work.

1.10.0.en: Thereby the name of our Lord Jesus Christ is glorified in the conduct of the people of Thessalonica, in their patience, obedience and faithfulness while they are on earth, and so they share with Him in His glories, a thing that no human being deserves, however great his holiness, but it is a generous gift to them from God and our Lord Jesus Christ.

1.10.1.en: Thus we see that the essential work of the Christian servant is to persevere in prayer for the spiritual growth of his children; so be careful, as a servant, or as a father or mother, to pray every day for those in your care. The man of sin and steadfastness in the faith

2.0.s.en: (1) The man of sin and the delay of his appearing

2.0.0.en: Spirit: A person who fixes the date of the Second Coming.

2.0.2.en: Letter as from us: A letter written by false teachers and not by the Apostles.

2.0.3.en: Concerning the day of the Second Coming and the gathering of mankind before Christ, Paul warns the people of Thessalonica not to believe the rumors and false teachings that fix the date. By this he means to establish them in the faith and to remove terror from them, so that they may devote themselves to worship and to carrying out their responsibilities calmly, because some false teachers exploited Paul's words in the first epistle about preparing for the Second Coming and fixed a date for it.

2.0.4.en: Let us not be preoccupied with the date of the Second Coming, for the end of our lives by death may come before it, and this can happen at any time. So let us be concerned instead with preparing for eternity through repentance and doing good, especially to those who wrong us.

2.1.0.en: Paul reaffirms his warning against the deception of the false teachers who fix a date for the Second Coming, and he gives two clear signs that occur before the coming of Christ, which are:

2.1.1.en: 1- A general apostasy, meaning that many believers deny and turn back from their faith in Christ, and not merely a few individuals as happens in every age.

2.1.2.en: 2- The revealing of the man of sin, by whom he means the Antichrist, whom he calls the son of perdition, who awaits dreadful eternal torment because he causes many to stumble and turns them away from the faith.

2.2.0.en: Among the characteristics of the man of sin is that he opposes God and exalts himself above all that is called God or is worshiped; this wicked person sits in the temple of God and prevents His worship, and claims to be God and that his station is above that of the true God, demanding for himself the honor and obedience that belong to God alone.

2.3.0.en: The Apostle Paul had already told them of this when he was with them, so he urges them to remember what was said to them before.

2.4.0.en: What restrains: The obstacles that God puts in place to prevent the revealing of the man of sin.

2.4.1.en: God does not allow the man of sin, that is, the Antichrist, to appear until the time appointed in God's mind comes, in order to give us an opportunity to prepare and to be steadfast in Him, and for the faith to spread throughout the whole world; so that if the man of sin arises and declares himself to be God and news of him spreads throughout the whole world, those who believe in Christ will not be shaken or be led after him.

2.5.0.en: The mystery of lawlessness: Satan, who works in secret in people's hearts to turn them away from God. Until he is taken out of the way who now restrains: God removes what prevents the Antichrist from appearing, that is, He allows him to appear.

2.5.1.en: St. Paul declares that although God now prevents the man of sin from appearing, God has permitted Satan to work, trying to turn His children away from Him by various evils, but at the same time the power of God supports them and establishes them. So now is an opportunity to discover the wiles of the devil and resist them, so that when the Antichrist appears, to whom Satan will give all his power, we may be strong and not be led astray after him.

2.6.0.en: The lawless one: The man of sin, that is, the Antichrist.

2.6.1.en: After the Antichrist appears to lead people astray, Christ will appear in His Second Coming and cast him into eternal torment.

2.7.s.en: (2) Satan works through the lawless one

2.7.0.en: Satan sends his agents to help the lawless one, that is, the "Antichrist", with all power, so he performs astonishing but false miracles, like those performed by Pharaoh's magicians.

2.8.0.en: The Antichrist will try to entice to evil those whose destiny is perdition, who are attracted to the teachings of that lawless one after rejecting the true teaching that comes from God.

2.9.0.en: God will permit Satan to spread error and deception, so the wicked, those not steadfast in the faith, and those who are superficial in their relationship with God will believe him and follow the Antichrist. But any person, however weak, who holds fast to the Church and to repentance, God will save, and He will condemn everyone who believed the teachings of the Antichrist and rejoiced in them.

2.9.1.en: Hold fast to the teachings of the Church and to your submission to your father of confession, so that evil may not dazzle you and no strange teaching may deceive you. And in proportion to your care for prayer, God will reveal evil to you and keep you away from it.

2.10.0.en: Sanctification of the Spirit: The setting apart of life by the Holy Spirit to belong to God.

2.10.1.en: Belief of the truth: Faith in Christ.

2.10.2.en: The Apostle thanks God for the faith of the people of Thessalonica and assures them that they are chosen by God and have known the faith, so that they may not be alarmed by the reports about the man of sin.

2.11.0.en: The thing to which He called you: Faith in Christ and the sanctification of life to Him. Our gospel: Our proclamation to you.

2.11.1.en: The glory of our Lord: Blessing in life on earth and then the eternal Kingdom. He explains the importance of the salvation to which He called them through his proclamation, so that they may obtain the Kingdom of Heaven.

2.12.0.en: The Apostle urges them to stand fast and hold to the teachings that they received, and not to be shaken on hearing the teaching that the false teachers introduced and that troubled them, namely that the day of the Lord had come.

2.12.1.en: In the original translation of the Gospel, "hold the traditions which ye have been taught"; this shows the importance of the oral tradition to which the Church holds, and this is also evident from the Apostle's saying in the same verse, "whether by word, or our epistle". And "word" is what is unwritten, that is, the oral tradition, which is added to what is written in his epistle.

2.13.0.en: Here the name of the Lord Jesus comes first, which shows the divinity of Christ and the equality of the hypostases.

2.13.1.en: St. Paul declares that God, who supported the people of Thessalonica in afflictions and gave them hope in the Kingdom in which He will reward them for their endurance, will remain with them, gladdening their hearts and establishing them in the faith before the false teachings around them, and making them grow in doing good.

2.13.2.en: Look at God's work and His support for you, so that your heart may be strengthened with thanksgiving to Him and you may grow in your love and service toward those around you, and in this way you will be fortified against the evils and strange ideas that Satan proclaims. The importance of work

3.0.s.en: (1) A request for their prayers and steadfastness

3.0.0.en: May run: The word of the Lord continues without hindrance like a flowing river.

3.0.1.en: Unreasonable and wicked men: The false teachers and the wicked who oppose Paul's proclamation. For all men have not faith: Sadly, there must be some who reject the faith because they cling to evil. Paul's humility appears in his asking the people of Thessalonica to pray for him and his disciples, and this for two matters:

3.0.2.en: 1- The continuation of the ministry and the preaching.

3.0.3.en: 2- The deliverance of Paul and the servants from the wicked opponents who must exist, since some insist on evil and therefore reject faith in Christ.

3.0.4.en: Here the importance of fellowship in prayer among the believers appears, the servants for those they serve and the reverse also.

3.1.0.en: After the Apostle has spoken of the wicked opponents who are unfaithful, he stresses the faithfulness of God, unlike men, for it is He who establishes the believers, keeps them from falling and protects them from the persecutions of those who trouble them.

3.2.0.en: Since they are united with Christ, the Holy Spirit will work in them so that they fulfil the commandments of Christ which they heard from Paul. From here comes the confidence of the Apostle Paul that as long as we "quench not the Spirit", the Spirit leads us to act on the commandments.

3.3.0.en: Satan tries to take our thoughts away from the love of God, exploiting circumstances of trial or sickness to whisper in the ears of the believer. Therefore the Apostle asks the Lord to awaken the hearts of the believers so that they perceive the love of God even in the depth of trial. And he gives them an example, which is the patience of Christ during His life on earth, and how many sorrows He endured, suffering wrongfully.

3.3.1.en: Sometimes the faith of some is shaken before pain, sickness or affliction, and they ask why a loving God permits trial for His children... May we humble ourselves before the divine wisdom and surrender our mind and our life to the Shepherd of the sheep and their Keeper, and trust in Him who suffered being tempted that He is able to help those who are tempted.

3.4.0.en: Disorderly: The divine order from the beginning was "In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread" (Gen 3:19), and before that the Lord God took Adam and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

3.4.1.en: The tradition: In the original Greek, "the tradition", that is, the oral teachings with which Paul charged them. In Thessalonica there were many who had stopped working and given themselves up to idleness on the pretext that they were awaiting the Second Coming of Christ, which they believed to be near. Therefore the Apostle Paul warns them about these people, and asks them to avoid them and shun them so that they may be ashamed of themselves and turn back from their way.

3.5.0.en: St. Paul asks the believers to imitate him, for he worked with his own hands among them so as not to burden them with providing for the expenses of his living; so much more should these idle people not depend on the Church to provide for their needs, but should work and depend on themselves.

3.6.0.en: It is the right of the pastors and consecrated servants that the Church provide for their material needs, but the Apostle did not make use of this right of his, in order to present to the believers a living example for them to follow.

3.7.0.en: If a person finds work but does not want to work, then the brethren are not required to help that person. This is an important principle that he had already charged them with when he was with them, and he wrote it in his first epistle to them and repeats it here a second time because of its importance. But if there is a person who is sick or cannot find work, then the believers must help him.

3.8.0.en: Busybodies: Those who do not work have empty minds, so they meddle in the affairs of others and trouble them by trying to find out their news.

3.8.1.en: Work with quietness: Keeping away from curiosity and much talking and the problems it causes. Their own bread: Let them provide for their material needs from the work of their hands.

3.8.2.en: Paul heard that some believers were idle and not working, disobeying what he had charged them, so he instructs these idle people to work and to keep away from trouble.

3.9.0.en: The Apostle now turns in his words to the others, who are constantly active in doing good and never tire of giving help to the needy, and he advises them to continue in their good works.

3.10.0.en: Note that man: Distinguish, set apart and make known this idle person so that you may shun him.

3.10.1.en: St. Paul commands the believers in the Church to punish the one who persists in not working by shunning him, so that perhaps he may be ashamed and repent and turn back from his stubbornness.

3.11.0.en: The believers must rebuke him for his fault, but in all love, and show him that they care for his good, for not associating with him is for the purpose of reforming him. Thus the offender should be treated with love and firmness, lest he perish.

3.11.1.en: Beware of idleness, for it begets many sins, and the holy Fathers advise the idle to remember the judgment, because God will call us to account for all our deeds and our wasting of time, and by this the fear of God and the pursuit of positive work are born in a person. So consider: to what extent do you use your time and invest your abilities for the glory of God and the service of others?

3.12.0.en: By all means: In all circumstances He satisfies all your spiritual, psychological and physical needs.

3.12.1.en: The Apostle asks God, the Lord of peace, to give them peace in every aspect of their life and to be with them.

3.13.0.en: The Apostle offers a greeting that he wrote personally with his own hand. It was his custom, because of his weak eyesight, to dictate his epistle to another person to write it, but he would conclude it at the end in his own handwriting as a sign of the authenticity of the epistle. For epistles had already appeared that were falsely attributed to him and that he had not in fact written.

3.14.0.en: As is his custom, St. Paul asks grace for all the believers in the Church.

3.14.1.en: Peace is the best thing that you can wish for all those around you and offer to them. So help them to hold fast to Christ, to leave sins, and to cast their problems at the feet of God in prayer so that they may regain their peace.
